questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Tonton, 10, was bitten on the leg by a stray dog an hour ago.
questions.stem: What is the FIRST thing to do for Tonton's bite wound?
options: Wash with soap and running water
questions.rationale: First aid for animal bites is to wash the wound with soap and water. An antiseptic such as povidone-iodine may then be applied.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Tonton, 10, was bitten on the leg by a stray dog an hour ago.
questions.stem: The owner of the biting dog is found. For how long should the dog be confined and observed?
questions.rationale: Any dog that has bitten a person is confined and observed for 10 to 14 days.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Rabies Prevention (PDF p. 182)
questions.quote: Confinement of any dog that has bitten a person for 10 to 14 days

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Why should there be no running water in the room of a client with rabies?
questions.rationale: Rabies (hydrophobia) causes painful throat spasms at the sight or sound of water. The client is not bathed and there is no running water in the room.
questions.quote: Patients should not be bathed and there should not be any running water in the room

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which test gives the MOST definitive diagnosis of rabies?
questions.rationale: The fluorescent rabies antibody test is the most definitive diagnosis. Negri bodies in the dog's brain also indicate rabies.
questions.quote: Fluorescent rabies antibody (RFA) – most definitive diagnosis

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Mang Pido, 60, stepped on a rusty nail a week ago. He now has trouble opening his mouth and a fixed grin.
questions.stem: Which disease is suspected in Mang Pido?
questions.rationale: Tetanus causes trismus (lockjaw), painful spasms of the chewing muscles, and risus sardonicus. Spores enter through dirty wounds.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Mang Pido, 60, stepped on a rusty nail a week ago. He now has trouble opening his mouth and a fixed grin.
questions.stem: What room environment is best for Mang Pido?
questions.rationale: The room is kept quiet and dim, and visitors are told not to stimulate the client, because stimuli can trigger spasms.
questions.quote: Keep the patient’s room quiet and dimply

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Mang Pido, 60, stepped on a rusty nail a week ago. He now has trouble opening his mouth and a fixed grin.
questions.stem: Which product neutralizes circulating tetanus toxin in Mang Pido?
questions.rationale: Treatment includes tetanus immunoglobulin (TIG), an antibiotic such as metronidazole, sedatives, and airway support.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.situation: Mang Pido, 60, stepped on a rusty nail a week ago. He now has trouble opening his mouth and a fixed grin.
questions.stem: How often should Mang Pido get a tetanus toxoid booster after recovery?
questions.rationale: Active immunization is maintained with a tetanus toxoid booster every 10 years.
questions.quote: booster dose of tetanus toxoid every 10 years

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A child with polio lets his head fall back when his shoulders are lifted. What is this sign?
questions.rationale: In polio, Hoyne sign is the head falling back when the shoulders are elevated. The tripod sign is sitting with arms extended behind for support.
questions.quote: Hoyne sign (head falls back when surprise and shoulders are elevated)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which pain medication should be AVOIDED in a client with polio?
questions.rationale: Analgesics are given, but not morphine, which depresses respiration in a client at risk of respiratory failure. Moist heat helps muscle pain.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which specimen is used for viral culture in suspected polio?
questions.rationale: Poliovirus spreads through oropharyngeal secretions and feces. Viral culture uses a stool sample.
